current_activity: Surrender: German delegation reaches the tactical headquarters on Lüneburg Heath at 11:30 and is refused
notes: Event date: 3 May 1945, 11:30 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 339). Event definition: The German delegation, led by General-Admiral von Friedeburg and General Kinzel, reaches Montgomery's tactical headquarters on Lüneburg Heath at 11:30 on 3 May and asks him to accept the surrender of three German armies withdrawing before the Russians; Montgomery refuses, but asks if they will surrender to him all German forces on his western and northern flanks, including Holland, Friesland, Heligoland, Schleswig-Holstein and Denmark; shown the military situation on Allied maps, the Germans agree to recommend this unconditional surrender to Field-Marshal Keitel, von Friedeburg takes the terms back that night, and Kinzel and a fourth member remain at Twenty-First Army Group headquarters (p. 339). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 339: "the delegation reached Montgomery's tactical head- quarters on Liineburg Heath at 11.30 a.m. on the 3rd"; "Von Friedeburg and another officer took the Allies' terms back to Keitel that night while Kinzel and a fourth member of the delegation remained at Twenty-First Army Group headquarters". Location: Timeloberg near Wendisch Evern (Lüneburg Heath), Niedersachsen (existing place PL0643) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the Timeloberg hill at Wendisch Evern, where the existing record C1202 (English Wikipedia) puts Montgomery's headquarters tent; Ellis names Lüneburg Heath only. current_activity: Surrender: German forces in Holland, north-west Germany, Schleswig-Holstein and Denmark surrender; signed at 18:30
notes: Event date: 4 May 1945, 18:30 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 339). Event definition: Von Friedeburg arrives back at Lüneburg Heath on the afternoon of 4 May and, in the presence of Press correspondents attached to Twenty-First Army Group, the Instrument of Surrender is signed at 18:30, to take effect from 08:00 on 5 May; it covers all German armed forces in Holland, in north-west Germany including the Frisian Islands and Heligoland, in Schleswig-Holstein and in Denmark, and all naval ships in these areas, which surrender unconditionally to the Commander-in-Chief of the Twenty-First Army Group; it is signed by Montgomery for the Allies and by von Friedeburg, Kinzel and others for the Germans (pp. 339-340). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 339: "the Instrument of Surrender was signed at 6.30 p.m., to take effect from 8.00 a.m. on May the 5th"; "Von Friedeburg arrived back at Liineburg Heath on the afternoon of the 4th". Location: Timeloberg near Wendisch Evern (Lüneburg Heath), Niedersachsen (existing place PL0643) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the Timeloberg hill at Wendisch Evern, where the existing record C1202 (English Wikipedia) puts Montgomery's headquarters tent; Ellis names Lüneburg Heath only. Location support: Ellis names Lüneburg Heath as the place of signing (p. 339); the point is the Timeloberg used in C1202. Commander: Field-Marshal Montgomery, who signed the instrument of surrender for the Twenty-First Army Group (Ellis, vol. II, p. 340). Context: The existing record C1202 (Army Group H, 4 May 1945) is the German side of the same signing; the two rows are not in conflict.
